The recipe I've been following for the rice is

3 cups uncooked shortgrain Rice

1/2 cup Seasoned Rice Vinegar (It must be rice vinegar, regular vinegar makes it nasty)

2 tablespoons Sugar

2 teaspoons Salt

To cook the rice -

First, rinse the rice.I find rinsing it keeps it from sticking to the pan, and from what I read it has something to do with removing excess starches. I rinse mine in cold water for about a minute or so, until the water strains clear.

For 3 cups of uncooked rice, I've been using about 3 1/4 cups of water.

Heat the water and rice until boiling, turn down to a simmer and cover until all water has evaporated (It's important that you try not to keep checking the rice, or else you'll let out all the steam and it won't cook properly. I suggest waiting at least 10-15 minutes before even checking... It depends on the size of pan you use I assume.)

Around this time I like to mix up my Rice vinegar with the sugar and salt. You can either heat it up in the microwave to help it dissolve some, or just let it soak. I've seen it done both ways. Just know if you heat it up, you will smell vinegar throughout your house.

Once there's no more water, keep pan covered and move pan away from heat. Let sit for at least another 10 minutes so that the rice can soak up all the moisture.

After the rice is done, move it to a glass or plastic bowl.

Make sure the Rice vinegar has cooled down if you decided to heat it up. Mix the Rice, and Rice Vinegar with a wooden spoon (metal spoons can have an adverse reaction to the vinegar) You can fan the Rice as you mix it to help it cool down.

As for the sushi recipe

You can really use any kind of ingredients you wish to. We've been using cooked shrimp and crab legs for now since we're beginners at making it.We also use cream cheese, sriracha and mayo mix, chopped green onions, Avocado, sliced cucumbers, and sliced carrots.

For the outside of the sushi you should get what's called "Nori" which is pretty much a seaweed wrap.

We went out and bought a little Bamboo Mat that you can use to roll the sushi, but I've read a small rag wrapped in plastic wrap could work just as well... I'm not sure though, I haven't tried. If you do have a bamboo mat, make sure to cover it in plastic wrap, or a ziplock baggy. It helps for clean up majorly.

To start the sushi, lay the Nori down on your mat, shiny side down.

Start putting some rice down on the Nori, making sure not to pat it down to much, just spread it evenly, making sure to leave at least 1/4 of the nori free from rice at the top. I'm guessing on measurements here, so bare with me. Also as a side note, it helps to have a bowl of cold water next to your rice, and dip your fingers in it each time you get more rice. It helps to keep the rice from getting to sticky.

Once you've gotten your rice down on the Nori, you can start adding your inner ingredients. Here's where you can really just improvise and make what you feel like. When you place them down you want to make sure you put your filling near the bottom of the rice, so it stays on the inside while rolling it. If you have any kind of sauce you want on it (I like sriracha and mayo mixed together) You might want to lay that down first, to keep the rest of the ingredients in place, and so that it doesn't get all over your fingers while rolling the sushi.

When you start to roll your sushi, start from the bottom up. I've read it helps to start it without the mat, but I tend to tear my Nori when I'm doing that. As your rolling, making sure to "tuck" underneath, to keep all the ingredients in place. Also, make sure to pull the mat up from time to time, so it doesn't get mixed in with the sushi. (I'm assuming you don't want to eat bamboo/wrag for dinner lol. )

When you're almost done wrapping the sushi, squish a few pieces of rice on the Nori that has no rice on it. This acts like a "glue" and helps keep the Nori stuck together.

Once your sushi roll is all nice and rolled up, you can either set aside, or cut it now. I like to make all mine and set them aside before I cut them.

To cut your sushi roll, you can lay a sheet of plastic wrap over the top to help keep everything in place, or you can cut it without it.

Make sure you have a sharp sharp sharp knife. It helps! Try and cut it with a dull knife and everything gets squished out of the roll.... I found that out the hard way. Anyways. When you have your knife nice and sharp, make sure to keep your knife clean and wet. Keeping it clean just helps, and keeping it wet helps keep the knife from sticking to the rice when you're cutting it. I keep a wet towel sitting next to me when I'm cutting the sushi to help out.

When you're done cutting the sushi, you can plate however you like! I like to put a little Unagi, or eel sauce, down on the plate first (just a drizzle) then top the sushi with a little Sriracha Mayo and a few drops of Soy Sauce.

And that's how I personally make sushi! I'm still a beginner, but I hope this helps you in your sushi ventures! If you'd like, next time I make sushi I'll take pictures of the progress and post them for you. :) Play around with the fillings. Even though I think "traditional" sushi tastes delicious, with the tuna and salmon and such, I believe anything wrapped in rice and Nori is sushi. But that's just my opinion man...

It was July 4th 1998. I was driving out to stay on my parent's house as we all do during the Fourth of July to stay for the weekend and play games and stuff. My wife and my two kids went first because I still have some work to do. After that, I went at around 12.35 PM.

But there was one peculiar thing. The highway was supposed to be in a heavy traffic jam, but this time it really wasn't. I thought maybe people went somewhere else?

I kept going on the highway when I noticed it was way too long. Until I noticed the exit. And there was a traffic jam! Great. It piled up here. It was too long, way too long. After what seems like an eternity it finally moved.

I drove forwards when I realized a highway. This is peculiar. They're probably building a new highway or something. Until I realized that it was the same highway as before.

"What the fuck?"

I drove, and look! The same exit. I went and the same traffic jam occurred! It went on and on and on. It was really weird. I called my wife to see what's up. They said I was a bit late. I am seriously scared. I went on and on until the highway turned red and it went dark. I looked at the time. It said 3.33 AM.

I was scared. I was on the highway again until I realized I can see what seems like shadows of people. Dark silhouettes. I am scared. I can hear the moaning, oh the moaning. It seems as if they were suffering. I can't take this anymore. I just closed my eyes and hoped for the best. The moaning was terrifying.

When I woke up, it was morning and I was on the front door of my parent's house. My wife and my cousins ran out.

"You were late. Seriously?"

I checked the time. 1.35 PM. It was only one hour. I was late by thirty minutes. What the fuck happened? Was I imagining it the whole time?

I just shrug it off as being me being tired and stayed at the house for the weekend. I thought everything was normal again.

tl;dr: Use countdown timers that increase with every suspicious action in order to stop people manipulating votes.

 

Vote manipulation is a problem with the Reddit-esque system of upvoting and downvoting. There's a few scenarios that can happen where one user and/or multiple accounts can make or break a post. The following is a few examples of said situations along with my proposed solutions.

 

Example #1: A single user upvotes or downvotes a bunch of different posts from one user.

In this case, a user's overall comment contribution points and/or submission contribution points could be inflated to give the appearance of popularity or good reputation. Alternatively, a user's comments or submissions could be buried to attain the opposite. A further level of manipulation is downvoting one person's posts while upvoting another person's posts in order to "stifle the competition".

My proposed solution for this is to have a sort of delay timer algorithm. The first handful of votes (in either direction) made by one account to another account would go fine. After, say, the third vote on the same user in a short period of time you are then presented with a delay message like "You must wait 1 minute to downvote/upvote that user's submissions again." Each successive vote adds to an overall "bank" of time, so someone attempting to give as much artificial help as possible or do as much damage as possible would be met with an increasingly frustrating wait. This message can be presented transparently to the user as a pop-up or something like that.

The downside is that a regular user may occasionally encounter the timer by upvoting or downvoting the same user through sheer chance. However, if their intent is not to specifically help or damage the SCP/CCP of one person this ought to be a rare situation.

 

Example #2: A single user makes multiple accounts to upvote or downvote the submissions/comments of one or more users, or multiple actual people collude to upvote/downvote submissons & comments.

This is the thing that got Unidan shadowbanned over at Reddit. He had like 5 alt accounts - he would have all of the alts upvote his comments and submissions while simultaneously using them to downvote his submissions. (The fact that he stuck around as long as he did without being shadowbanned probably means that Reddit's automated detection for this stuff is lackluster on the backend.)

This scenario is bad because it allows one person with multiple accounts to decide content. In most Reddit-style voting systems, the first few upvotes or downvotes count a lot. Anyone who's been on Reddit can tell you how difficult it is to recover even from something as tiny as -5 karma on a post.

It could also be abused by companies as seen with Quickmeme - there was a bot running on /r/adviceanimals that would upvote Quickmeme posts and downvote posts from similar competing services. Quickmeme gets the traffic and the other businesses don't; submissions were not honestly being voted on solely on their merit as a post (well, as far as an advice animal can have merit as a post, anyway).

The solution to this is similar to the solution to #1 - a delay timer based on repeated behavior. If multiple accounts are voting in quick succession the same way (such as 5 accounts all upvoting a post within a few minutes) and these multiple accounts have a similar pattern of behavior (that is, these 5 accounts all upvote or downvote a certain post within a certain time period repeatedly), then it ought to be assumed that this is a single person (or a group of people) acting in bad faith to manipulation submissions and comments one way or another. If this all comes from the same IP address and constantly vote the same way then they ought to be considered alts made by the same person and put on a delay much quicker. If they come from different IPs, the delay ought to be a bit more relaxed (giving the benefit of the doubt that it's only coincidence).

If they are upvoting or downvoting the same person too much they should be met with a message like that in Example #1. If they are simply engaged in group voting behavior, then they ought to have an account-wide delay on upvoting or downvoting that increases in severity with the increase of frequency of votes.

The downside would be people rarely being caught up in this system, but it's really unlikely that they would be caught up in this system by accident.

This system could even be extended to combat bot networks to some degree if it were properly designed in specific terms.

 

I think a delay timer that operates as described here would be a successful mechanism for combating vote manipulation while simultaneously minimizing collateral damage. Vote manipulation can get you shadowbanned (with no warning, of course) over at Reddit. Someone shouldn't lose an account because they accidentally voted on a post or two of one of their alts without thinking, but they also simultaneously shoudn't be able to use multiple accounts to manipulate the system.

What are your thoughts on this? Please poke holes into my idea or bring up other scenarios where this may not work. I sincerely believe the idea has merit.
